title: Support local at the outdoor Kitchener Market on July 25
content: The Kitchener Market will be open this Saturday, July 25, with an outdoor market experience in the Breezeway featuring local farmers, makers and vendors.

While recovery efforts continue inside the Market building, we're pleased to provide an opportunity for the community to shop local and support vendors. Visitors can expect many of the familiar vendors that make the Kitchener Market a community favourite, offering fresh produce, packaged foods and unique local products.

The Kitchener Market has long been an important gathering place and a vital support for local farmers, small businesses and entrepreneurs. We encourage residents to come out, shop local and support the vendors who help make the Market such a special part of our community.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener media@kitchener.ca

title: Registration is now open for Kitchener’s 3rd annual Paddle Palooza Pickleball Festival
content: Get ready to hit the courts in Downtown Kitchener as the City of Kitchener’s Paddle Palooza Pickleball Festival returns to Carl Zehr Square on Tuesday, August 25 from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.
Whether you're a seasoned player or new to the game, Paddle Palooza offers friendly competition, learn to play courts, great prizes, and high-energy vibes all day long.
The tournament, presented in partnership with Four Fathers Brewing and Four Fathers Pickleball, offers the following divisions, limited to six teams each:
Men’s Doubles (50+)
Ladies’ Doubles (50+)
Mixed Doubles (18+)
Ladies’ Doubles (18+)
Adult / Youth (under 18) Doubles *NEW*

Registration is now open at  Kitchener.ca/pickleball. The cost to register a team in the tournament is $50 per team with a limit of six teams per division. All other street play is free. Proceeds from the tournament will support the city’s Every Kid Counts program, helping to make camp an option for children and youth in Kitchener by providing inclusion support.

Not quite ready for tournament play or just want to enjoy the game of pickleball? Paddle Palooza will celebrate all levels of pickleball skill and interest, ranging from curious to competitive. Join the free drop-in s treet play (3 courts), learn-to-play, and pick up some tips & tricks. Come out and give pickleball a try.  Spectators are welcome and encouraged. Whether you're playing or just soaking up the vibes, there's something for everyone. Come for the tournament, stay for the fun, including drop-in games, family activities, vendor booths, food trucks, a beer garden and more.

Pickleball is a hybrid paddle sport that combines elements of tennis, badminton, and ping pong, and is experiencing a rapid rise in popularity across Canada, reaching over one million Canadians (Pickleball Canada, 2023). The City of Kitchener has also seen significant growth and interest in the sport in recent years at community centres and outdoor courts.
For more information, or to register a team, visit Kitchener.ca/pickleball .

title: Beloved local restaurant selected to bring a major flavour boost to the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park
content: The City of Kitchener has selected  Almadina, a long-standing, family-run Kitchener business with more than 30 years in the community, to  operate the on-site food service at the new Cowan Recreation Centre, located at RBJ Schlegel park and  opening late this year.

Almadina was chosen following a competitive process that emphasized fresh, nutritious and locally sourced food, diverse and inclusive menu offerings, strong customer experience and a commitment to sustainable operations, including responsible sourcing and waste reduction.

Centrally  located within the Cowan Recreation Centre, the on-site food service will support the facility’s role as a landmark recreation destination for residents, families, athletes and sport tourism events. The menu will include a wide variety of options such as smoothies and juices, flatbread pizzas, breakfast wraps and pastries, chicken club sandwiches, falafel wraps, build-your-own bowls, samosas, grab-and-go snacks and kid-friendly options.

“We’re thrilled to welcome  Almadina to the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park ,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “Supporting local businesses is essential to building a strong, resilient economy, and  Almadina is a great example of the entrepreneurial spirit that makes Kitchener special. For more than 30 years, this family-run business has been part of our community, and now they’ll help fuel a landmark recreation centre designed for everyone to connect, compete and belong.”

Almadina operates four locations in Waterloo Region, including at the Kitchener Market, and is known for fresh, healthy Mediterranean-inspired food made with locally sourced ingredients whenever possible. Their commercial kitchen allows them to scale production to meet the demands of tournaments, events and busy periods at the Cowan Recreation Centre.

“This community has supported us for decades, and we’re excited to bring our fresh menu and our commitment to great customer experience to a space that will serve families, athletes and visitors in the years to come,” said  Abdullah Lawendy, owner of  Almadina. “We look forward to offering food that is healthy,  flavourful and made with care.”

When the facility opens late this year, the on-site food service is expected to  operate 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. seven days a week. The first year of operation will act as a pilot period to monitor demand and adjust hours as needed to support sustainable operations and accessible pricing.
Almadina will also offer catering for meetings and events inside the facility and will introduce seasonal menu rotations as the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park  grows and evolves.
For updates and more information, visit  Kitchener.ca/crc.
For more information:
Corporate Communications and Marketing  City of Kitchener  media@kitchener.ca

title: City of Kitchener directs first water allocation to affordable housing and priority community projects
content: The  City of Kitchener has received its first municipal water servicing capacity allocation from the Region of Waterloo and will use its recently approved Water Allocation Policy to advance housing and community-building projects that deliver the greatest benefit to residents.

The City has been  allocated 11.43 litres per second of municipal water servicing capacity for the third quarter of 2026. This first allocation will support affordable and supportive housing, community infrastructure , and other priority developments that align with Kitchener's new Official Plan and the needs of a growing city.

In June, Kitchener City Council approved the Water Allocation Policy in response to regional water supply constraints. The policy provides a transparent and consistent framework for directing available servicing capacity to projects that advance housing affordability, community infrastructure, employment  growth, and complete communities, while supporting the goals of the  City’s Official Plan.

"This allocation is about making sure available water capacity is directed to projects that deliver the greatest benefit to our community," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "By prioritizing affordable housing, essential services and other strategic community investments, we're addressing today's needs while advancing the long-term vision of our new Official Plan."

Beginning this week, City staff will  start  issuing water servicing capacity  to eligible developments. Staff anticipate that all Priority 1 projects can proceed, including affordable and supportive housing developments being delivered in partnership with other levels of government.
The current intake includes proposals that would house more than 7,100 people  and provide  3,740 square  metres ( 40,000 square feet) of employment and commercial space.
Key projects will include:

Reception House Wellington Street North  –  creating 34 new transitional housing units for government-assisted, newly arrived Canadians, ensuring affordability for  families and individuals as they transition to a life in their new community. In addition to the City providing land, Reception House received a $300,000 grant through the City’s Not-for-profit affordable rental and co-op housing incentive program, supported through the Housing Accelerator Fund program.
Fire Station 8 and Housing Development – delivering improved emergency services for the City and 281 below-market and market-rate rental units

This allocation  represents the first round under both the Region of Waterloo's municipal allocation process and Kitchener's Water Allocation Policy. Additional allocation rounds are anticipated as more servicing capacity becomes available.

The  City  remains committed to careful  and sustainable  management of available water resources and is confident that future allocations, together with the Region's long-term framework, will support the housing and development needed to meet Kitchener's evolving community needs over the coming decades.
Learn more  about the Water Allocation Policy .
About the City’s New Official Plan

Council has approved the City of Kitchener’s new Official Plan,  developed following  public engagement with thousands of residents for Kitchener 205 .  The new plan will guide how Kitchener grows over the coming decades, supporting housing, transportation, climate resilience, economic development, and complete communities. The Official Plan  has been  submitted to the Province of Ontario for approval before coming into effect.

The new Official Plan focuses on strengthening  neighbourhoods, increasing housing options and affordability, and making it easier, safer, and more sustainable for residents to access the places and spaces that matter most.
Learn more about the Official Plan and Kitchener 2051 on our website.
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener media@kitchener.ca

title: Drowning Prevention Week - July 19 to 25
content: Over 400 Canadians die in preventable water-related incidents annually. Even one drowning is one too many. The Lifesaving Society designates the third week in July as National Drowning Prevention Week. During the week of July 19 to 26, 2025 , our pools will offer resources and awareness programs to help keep you and your family stay safe all year long.
On this page:

This year’s theme, “Prepare to be Water Smart” aims to teach Ontarians the simple steps they can take to prevent drowning and water-related injury by preparing themselves to be in, on, and around the water.

Water safety information and activity sheets related to drowning prevention and swim safety will be offered during National Drowning Prevention Week , July 19 to 25, 2026, at all City of Kitchener pool locations.
Join us for a Toonie Swim and enjoy our new wibits and climbing wall, interactive water safety booths, special guests and a chance to win a 2027 Summer Splash Pass.
Lanes are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Admission is $2.
Date: Friday, July 24
Time: 12:30 p.m. to 4:15 p.m.
Location: Harry Class Pool, 45 Woodside Ave.
Register in advance on ActiveNet .
Date: Saturday, July 25, 2026

The World Health Organization (WHO) recognizes World Drowning Prevention Day on July 25. It serves as an opportunity to highlight the tragic and profound impact of drowning on families and communities and offers lifesaving solutions to prevent it.
·  Wear blue in recognition
·  City of Kitchener City Hall and Kitchener Memorial Auditorium light up in blue in recognition
·  Learn more: World Drowning Prevention Day
Learn more at Lifesaving Society | Resources
It’s summertime, which means the Kitchener Swims penguin is ready to have some fun in the sun! Help Penny the Penguin prepare for a safe and fun summer near the water with this coloring sheet.
Submit the colouring sheet to any City of Kitchener pool by Friday, July 31, 2026 . Include your name and contact information to be entered into a draw to win a free 2027 Summer Splash Pass!

Two winners will be selected and contacted in the Spring of 2027. Entries must be submitted by Friday, July 31, 2026 at any of the City of Kitchener pool locations. One submission per person. There is no age limit to participate.

title: Help Shape the Future of Transportation in Kitchener
content: Should Kitchener invest more in safer walking and cycling connections? Improve transit reliability? Target traffic pinch points?
These are some of the key recommendations emerging from the City's draft Transportation and Mobility Plan and now residents are being asked if we're on the right track.

The way we move through our neighbourhoods and across our city plays an important role in our quality of life. Whether walking, cycling, taking transit or driving, the infrastructure we plan and build has a direct impact on safety, accessibility and how connected we feel to our community.
The City of Kitchener is committed to creating a Connected City, guided by our vision of building a city for everyone where, together, we take care of the world around us - and each other.

To help achieve that vision, the City launched Connected Kitchener to develop a new Transportation and Mobility Plan. The plan is designed to ensure Kitchener's transportation network continues to meet the needs of residents today while preparing for the future.
More than 600 residents have already shared their experiences, challenges and ideas for getting around Kitchener.  Based on that feedback, the City has developed draft recommendations that focus on:
As the project enters its next phase, the City is looking for residents to review these recommendations and help identify what matters most when it comes to moving around the community.
Residents are encouraged to review the draft plan recommendations and complete the online survey at https://www.engagewr.ca/ConnectedKitchener

While the Transportation and Mobility Plan focuses on areas under the City of Kitchener's responsibility, it will also align closely with the Region of Waterloo's transportation initiatives. By working together, both levels of government can advance shared goals and create a more coordinated transportation network for the community.

Building an integrated mobility system that supports the movement of both people and goods is essential to creating a connected, healthy and inclusive city. Community feedback will help shape the final plan and ensure it reflects the needs and priorities of Kitchener residents for years to come.
Learn more, review the draft plan recommendations and share your feedback at: https://www.engagewr.ca/ConnectedKitchener
